summary: 'What is F-Line Appeal?' (service code 0185) is answered as 'What is F-Line?' (service code 0178) -- a different, real code silently swapped for another one.
preconditions: No upload needed -- a plain chat question, officer marun_chn@sis.tn.gov.in (SIS-002).
reproduction: 1. Send: 'What is F-Line?' -> correctly answers service code 0178.
2. Send: 'What is F-Line Appeal?' -> answers service code 0178 again, verbatim identical text to step 1, never mentioning 0185.
3. Send: 'What is the difference between F-Line and F-Line Appeal?' -> again answers only 0178, states no difference, never names 0185 at all.
expected: Step 2 should answer service code 0185 'F-Line Appeal'. Step 3 should explain both 0178 and 0185 and their difference.
actual: All three questions return: 'Service code 0178 = F-Line (Urban Demarcation) (F_LINE) -- TAMILNILAM urban service, field visit required. Files under it are held in your register.'
root_cause: backend/utils/helpers.py `_svc_name_alias_match()` (line ~299) matches the bare substring 'f-line'/'f line'/'fline' anywhere in the message and returns 0178 immediately. It runs BEFORE `find_service_code_by_name()`'s keyword-overlap scoring (which weighs 'Appeal' as a distinctive word of 0185's name) ever gets a chance to run, so 'F-Line Appeal' never reaches that scoring at all.
verified_outcome: CONFIRMED live through the chatbot UI, 2026-10-13. Regression test: SIS_ServiceCode_FileDB_Regression_Tests/test_servicecode_alias_collision.py (fails on current code, 2 of 3 cases, no DB/LLM needed).
evidence_source: live browser session, chatbot.html, officer marun_chn@sis.tn.gov.in, 2026-10-13 ~12:09-12:10

summary: 'List all the service codes in this file.' on an uploaded CSV with a service_code column is refused with 'I could not find this in the uploaded document.', even though the column exists and the equivalent literal phrasing answers correctly.
preconditions: sis_svccode_fileA.csv attached (header: row, service_code, service_description, application_number, status; 5 data rows).
reproduction: 1. Upload sis_svccode_fileA.csv.
2. Send: 'List all the service codes in this file.' -> 'I could not find this in the uploaded document.'
3. Send: 'list the service_code column' -> correctly returns all 5 rows' service_code values with citation.
expected: Step 2 and step 3 should both deterministically list the service_code column's 5 values (0154, 0178, 0158, 0153, 0154).
actual: Step 2 is refused outright (the ungrounded retrieval/evidence-floor refusal); step 3 (same column, exact header name quoted) succeeds.
root_cause: csv_ops.resolve_column() requires the normalised header text to appear in the question bounded by a trailing non-alphanumeric boundary; the header 'service_code' normalises to 'service code', but the natural plural 'service codes' fails that boundary (the 's' is alphanumeric). The fallback single-distinctive-word match then finds TWO columns sharing the word 'service' (service_code AND service_description), so resolve_column() returns None rather than guessing -- and parse_csv_question() returns None as a result, so the question never reaches the deterministic CSV engine at all.
verified_outcome: CONFIRMED live through the chatbot UI, 2026-10-13. Regression test: SIS_ServiceCode_FileDB_Regression_Tests/test_csv_plural_column_resolution.py (fails on current code, 2 of 3 cases, no DB/LLM needed).
evidence_source: live browser session, chatbot.html, officer marun_chn@sis.tn.gov.in, 2026-10-13 ~12:11-12:12

summary: 'Compare the service codes in both files.' across two attached CSVs does not go through the deterministic multi-CSV comparison path at all (same root cause as CSVCOL-001a); it falls to the ungrounded LLM path, which then states WRONG per-file values for one of the two files.
preconditions: sis_svccode_fileA.csv AND sis_svccode_fileB.csv both attached (File A rows: 0154,0178,0158,0153,0154 across 5 rows; File B rows: 0178,0164,0154,01778,0160 across 5 rows -- independently established ground truth, SIS_File_Position_Ground_Truth.json).
reproduction: 1. Upload sis_svccode_fileA.csv, then sis_svccode_fileB.csv.
2. Send: 'Compare the service codes in both files.'
-> 'The service codes in file A are 0154, 0154, 0158, 0153, 0154. The service codes in file B are 0178, 0164, 0154, 01778, 0160.'
expected: File A's codes stated as 0154, 0178, 0158, 0153, 0154 (row 2's 0178 included, 0154 appearing exactly twice), via the deterministic `render_multi_csv_result` path, never the LLM.
actual: File B's figures are correct (0178, 0164, 0154, 01778, 0160, matching ground truth exactly), but File A's are wrong: 0178 (csv_row 2) is silently DROPPED, and 0154 is stated THREE times instead of two -- numbers that were never computed from the CSV rows, i.e. a narrated/hallucinated count rather than the deterministic answer CLAUDE.md's 'CSV questions are computed, not narrated' rule requires.
root_cause: Same as CSVCOL-001a: `csv_ops.parse_csv_question('Compare the service codes in both files.', ...)` returns None for BOTH files (verified directly), so `attachment_qa.py`'s `len(csv_docs) >= 2` deterministic branch (`per_doc_results` stays empty) never produces an answer and the question falls through to the ungrounded LLM/retrieval path. The LLM was then handed the raw CSV text of both files as evidence and wrote its own (wrong, for File A) summary -- exactly the uncomputed-numbers failure mode the project's CSV architecture exists to prevent, reached here only because the column-resolution bug routed the question around it.
verified_outcome: CONFIRMED live through the chatbot UI, 2026-10-13 -- a single root cause (CSVCOL-001) with two distinct, independently reproduced symptoms. Fixing resolve_column()'s plural/ambiguity gap (CSVCOL-001a) should also close this one, since both questions would then reach the deterministic engine; this was NOT verified because no fix was applied (initial audit only, per task instructions).
evidence_source: live browser session, chatbot.html, officer marun_chn@sis.tn.gov.in, 2026-10-13 ~12:13; cross-checked with a direct `csv_ops.parse_csv_question()` call returning None for the same question text against both files' headers

summary: 'Don't explain. Just give me the F-Line service code.' returns the full standard explanation sentence, identical to an unrestricted 'What is F-Line?' -- the brevity/no-explanation instruction is silently ignored.
preconditions: No upload needed -- a plain chat question.
reproduction: 1. Send: 'Don't explain. Just give me the F-Line service code.'
-> 'Service code 0178 = F-Line (Urban Demarcation) (F_LINE) -- TAMILNILAM urban service, field visit required. Files under it are held in your register.'
expected: A short answer naming only the code (e.g. '0178'), honouring the explicit 'don't explain' instruction.
actual: The full one-sentence explanation (name, category, field-visit requirement, register note) is returned -- the same text the brief, unrestricted question already returns.
root_cause: `_service_code_lookup_answer()` / `describe_service_code(..., brief=True)` in backend/services/chatbot.py and backend/utils/helpers.py have exactly ONE non-detailed output shape (the one-sentence 'brief' form), which is already a full explanatory sentence -- there is no code path capable of returning just the bare code, and no caller reads a brevity/format-restriction cue from the message at all before calling it. This is a gap in capability, not a missed branch of an existing one.
verified_outcome: CONFIRMED live through the chatbot UI, 2026-10-13.

summary: 'I don't think so.' sent right after an ordinary (non-attachment) factual answer gets a generic, unrelated clarification message instead of addressing the disputed claim -- the project's own negative-correction handling (is_negative_correction / _handle_negative_correction) is scoped only to an ACTIVE attachment conversation.
preconditions: No upload active at the point of the disputed statement (prior turn was the plain DB-backed F-Line/BREVITY-001 answer).
reproduction: 1. Send: 'Don't explain. Just give me the F-Line service code.' -> gets the full F-Line 0178 explanation (see BREVITY-001).
2. Send: 'I don't think so.'
-> 'I'm not sure what you mean. Please ask about an application, survey number, service, field visit, or workflow.'
expected: Per the task's own Phase 6 requirement for 'an ordinary factual explanation that did not ask a yes/no question': determine what is disputed and verify the evidence where possible, or at minimum ask a FOCUSED clarification referencing the disputed statement.
actual: A totally generic, topic-blind fallback message that does not reference F-Line, the service code, or anything said in the previous turn -- indistinguishable from what any unparseable message gets.
root_cause: grep across backend/services/chatbot.py, rag.py and neg_scope.py finds exactly one handler for a disagreement/correction phrase ('I don't think so' / 'not that' / 'wrong answer' etc.): `attachment_qa.is_negative_correction()` + `_handle_negative_correction()`, and every call site in chatbot.py gates it behind `attachment_topic_active(db, session_id)` or a prior attachment-turn check. There is no equivalent handling anywhere in the ordinary (non-attachment) conversation path, so a disputed database-backed or service-code answer falls through to the plain 'I'm not sure what you mean' catch-all.
verified_outcome: CONFIRMED live through the chatbot UI, 2026-10-13, and independently confirmed by the grep (no other call site exists).
evidence_source: live browser session, chatbot.html, officer marun_chn@sis.tn.gov.in, 2026-10-13 ~12:15; grep of backend/services/{chatbot,rag,neg_scope}.py

summary: Typing the EXACT attached filename 'sis_svccode_fileA.csv' (copied verbatim from the bot's own 'Attached here: ...' listing) is echoed back by the bot as 'sis_svccode_filed.csv' ('fileA' silently rewritten to 'filed') and rejected as not attached.
preconditions: sis_svccode_fileA.csv and sis_svccode_fileB.csv both attached; the bot had just asked 'Which one do you mean?' and listed both filenames verbatim.
reproduction: 1. With both files attached, send: 'Is sis_svccode_fileA.csv relevant to our project?'

2. Send the bare disambiguation question: 'Is this document relevant to our project?' -> bot correctly asks 'You have 2 files attached ... Which one do you mean?'
3. Reply with the EXACT filename it just listed: 'sis_svccode_fileA.csv'
-> SAME mangled-filename refusal as step 1: '"sis_svccode_filed.csv" is not attached ...'
expected: The filename as typed (byte-for-byte identical to the attachment list the bot itself printed) should match the attached document.
actual: Some pre-processing step rewrites the trailing 'A.csv' of 'fileA.csv' to 'd.csv', producing 'filed.csv', which then fails the attachment lookup -- reproducible on 2 of 2 attempts with the identical filename text.
root_cause: NOT fully pinned down in this pass (static root-causing was not performed for this one, to stay within scope) -- most likely a typo-correction / fuzzy-token pass (e.g. `_fragment_typo_fix` or a similar dictionary-based corrector elsewhere in the message-preprocessing chain) treating the short token 'filea' as a probable typo of the real English word 'filed' and silently 'fixing' it before the filename-matching logic ever runs. Suspected location: wherever chatbot.py / followup_context.py runs a typo-fix pass on the raw message BEFORE attachment_store.mentions_filename() / attachment_qa.mentions_filename() compares it against the attached filenames.
verified_outcome: CONFIRMED live through the chatbot UI, 2026-10-13, reproduced twice with the identical filename. Root cause location is a SUSPECTED area, not confirmed by code inspection in this pass -- flagged as a follow-up investigation.

summary: 'What is on line 10?' against an uploaded .txt file does not answer with line 10's content -- it dumps the entire document (all lines) as a table, mislabelled 'lines 1-10' / '5 records' for an 8-line body.
preconditions: sis_lineposition_test.txt attached (10 physical lines, ground truth independently established in SIS_File_Position_Ground_Truth.json BEFORE upload: line 10 = 'Final line contains the known value: LAST-LINE-VALUE-ALPHA-999.').
reproduction: 1. Upload sis_lineposition_test.txt.
2. Send: 'In sis_lineposition_test.txt, what is on line 10?'
-> returns a table titled 'sis_lineposition_test.txt, lines 1-10' / '5 records', whose FIELD/DETAILS rows are the file's 8 non-empty lines concatenated in order -- not line 10 in isolation.
expected: A direct answer naming only line 10's content: 'Final line contains the known value: LAST-LINE-VALUE-ALPHA-999.'

summary: The new 'project relevance' attachment feature (is_project_relevance_request / _build_project_relevance_assessment in attachment_qa.py) generates large blocks of pre-written Tamil/English prose, selected purely by filename/heading SUBSTRING matching (e.g. 'template', 'pitch', 'hackathon' in the filename or headings), asserting specific confident claims (e.g. 'Highly relevant for demonstrating the cost-effectiveness... of the SIS AI Assistant') that are never checked against the uploaded document's actual content -- a pattern the project's own architecture explicitly forbids elsewhere ('No evidence, no LLM', CLAUDE.md Chat Attachments section).
preconditions: Static code review of the Initial Commit diff to backend/services/attachment_qa.py (lines ~364-876, the project-relevance block).
reproduction: Code inspection: `_build_project_relevance_assessment()` branches on `is_template = any(w in fname_low for w in ("template","pitch","deck",...))` and similar heading-substring checks, then returns one of ~4 large HARDCODED paragraphs (in both English and Tamil) that name specific technologies ('FastAPI, PostgreSQL, local Ollama LLM') and make evaluative claims about the SIS project -- none of which come from the uploaded document's extracted text, only from its filename and section headings.

Attempted live reproduction with an unrelated CSV (sis_svccode_fileA.csv) was BLOCKED by FNAME-001 and ORDCLAR-001 (could not get the clarify-files flow to resolve to a specific file in this pass) -- so the actual rendered hallucination text was not captured live this pass; this finding rests on code inspection, not a captured transcript.
expected: A relevance assessment should be grounded in the document's actual retrieved content (per the project's own 'no evidence, no LLM' rule for every other attachment answer), or should explicitly decline to assess a document whose content was not retrieved/verified.
actual: The code path can assert specific, confident claims (e.g. 'cost-effectiveness... of the SIS AI Assistant', 'highly relevant') driven only by a filename or heading keyword match, with no check that the claim is actually true of that specific document's content.
root_cause: backend/services/attachment_qa.py, `_build_project_relevance_assessment()` (added this commit) -- branches entirely on `is_template` / `is_cadastral` / `csv_data` boolean flags derived from filename and heading substrings, then returns fixed prose blocks rather than text built from retrieved evidence chunks the way every other attachment answer in this file is required to be.
verified_outcome: NOT independently verified live this pass (blocked by FNAME-001/ORDCLAR-001). Flagged from code inspection as a confirmed architectural inconsistency (the code unambiguously does this), with the actual hallucinated output text itself unconfirmed live -- reported as a suspected/plausible live-behaviour defect, not a confirmed one, per the task's own instruction to separate the two.
